name: Felix
overview: The Scripture presents Felix as the Roman governor before whom Paul was brought after being rescued from a Jewish mob, as detailed in Claudius Lysias' letter (Acts 23:24-27). Although Paul was accused by the Jews, Lysias found no charges deserving death or imprisonment (Acts 23:28-29). This account highlights Felix's role in overseeing Paul's trial, during which he was notably unsettled by Paul's preaching, yet he chose to keep Paul in custody rather than release him.
